proposition: According to Melvin-Koushki, Ibn Turka's legacy was partly obscured in late Timurid Iran by Jami's revisionism (countered by the Kashifis' lettrist writings), and by the mid-11th/17th century Safavid memory appears to have reduced him to an important intellectual and a failed Sufi; the 11th/17th-century Dabistan used him strictly as an authority on illuminationist philosophy.
